description: A loan portfolio manager must decide whether to renew a manufacturing company's revolving credit line and finalize its availability, borrower funding condition, cash-control trigger, and compliance controls, with input from risk, relationship management, legal, and compliance.

shared_context.S1: Northstar Components is asking the bank to renew its $20,000,000 revolving credit line for another twelve months.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the binding renewal decision.
shared_context.S3: The borrower reported positive operating cash flow for the last four quarters and has made all scheduled interest payments on time.
shared_context.S4: The draft renewal package keeps the full $20,000,000 availability, contains no borrower cash-funding condition, and does not specify any special cash-control or compliance terms.
shared_context.S5: At the renewal meeting, the portfolio manager routinely takes a review from risk, relationship management, legal, and compliance before finalizing the package.

PF1.text: Harish completed the borrowing-base review this morning and confirmed that only $14,000,000 of Northstar's inventory and receivables is eligible collateral under the current advance rates; the updated worksheet has not yet been uploaded to the renewal file.

PF2.text: Maya received the signed sponsor letter yesterday confirming that Northstar's owners will inject exactly $3,000,000 of new equity at renewal closing; she has not yet attached the letter to the credit package.

PF3.text: Jonas found in the existing intercreditor agreement while reviewing the file this week that cash dominion must begin whenever revolver utilization exceeds 75% of the committed availability; the legal condition is not stated in the draft amendment.

PF4.text: Tara confirmed in a compliance memo received this morning that the renewal may proceed only with a beneficial-ownership certification completed before the first post-renewal draw and refreshed annually; the control has not yet been added to the renewal checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The revolving credit line must be renewed.
The renewal must require exactly $3,000,000 of new equity at closing.
Cash dominion must begin when utilization exceeds 75% of committed availability.
A beneficial-ownership certification must be required before the first post-renewal draw and annually thereafter.
The settlement must include commitments for the equity injection, cash dominion, and beneficial-ownership certification.
The $14,000,000 eligible-collateral finding must be cited as justification.

decisive_facts.why: The public draft offers the full $20,000,000 line, while PF1 changes maximum_availability_usd to exactly $14,000,000 because that is the confirmed eligible-collateral amount.
The public package has no borrower funding condition, while PF2 changes the renewal from an unsupported full line to an approved renewal requiring exactly $3,000,000 of equity at closing.
The draft contains no cash-control trigger, while PF3 changes the legal package to require cash dominion once utilization exceeds exactly 75% of committed availability.
The draft contains no special compliance control, while PF4 changes the renewal package to require beneficial-ownership certification before the first post-renewal draw and annually thereafter.
